Stats at capture: 59 replies; likes/views not exposed by the syndication API this pass. Quotes @MichaelThiessen (posted 12:58Z same day) — the quoted tweet carries the method.

## Summary

Pocock amplifies Thiessen's experiment: **Jev as a fuzzy linter that runs after edits in your agent harness**. Thiessen's recipe (captured text truncated mid-sentence): convert all coding guidelines into "tiny rules that are very easy to judge," then keep only the ones that don't require full-scale intelligence to evaluate. Pocock's endorsement adds the key framing: *some rules are too complex to lint deterministically but feel wasted on a full-scale model* — his examples: using useEffect sensibly; keeping good comments while killing bad ones.

## Why it matters

- **Fourth Jev data point, and the pattern is now unmistakable.** [[2026-09-17-anthdm-jev-agent-memory]] (memory triage), [[2026-09-19-altryne-jev-instant-compaction]] (context compaction), [[2026-09-20-rbilgil-jev-realtime-slop-detector]] (feed scoring) — every one is the same shape: a tiny model making cheap judgments on discrete items *before* they cost something scarce. Thiessen's version points it at *code after an agent edit*, before a human review or a big-model pass.
- **Pocock's "wasted on full-scale intelligence" is the economic argument stated cleanly.** Deterministic linters can't judge taste; frontier models shouldn't be paid to. The middle tier — rules easy to judge, hard to encode — is exactly what a small classifier is for. Same cost-tiering logic as [[2026-09-17-agrawal-agent-simplification-prompts]] (don't spend model capability where rules suffice).
- **Complements, not replaces, numeric gates.** [[2026-09-01-quentin-cody-code-quality-gates]] keeps measurable slop out by threshold; this catches the fuzzy residue (bad comments, awkward hooks) that gates can't express. A mature harness plausibly runs both: deterministic gates first, fuzzy-lint second, human third.
- **Relevant lens for our own pipelines:** our capture flow already uses "easy to judge" rules (wikilink verification, frontmatter checks). A fuzzy-lint pass over agent-written notes before commit is the same move at our scale.
- **Skepticism gates:** Thiessen's tweet truncates before the eval results ("looks very promising so far in my evals" is all we get — no numbers, no repo from either author). "Promising in my evals" on self-graded guidelines is weak evidence; false-positive rate on judgment calls is exactly where these systems rot. Endorsement by Pocock raises visibility, not validity.
